body:
Staring deeply at your monitor, you are trying to
come up with a new design for your school club
poster. You make some samples, but you aren’t
happy with any of them. You stand up, do some
stretches, and sit down again. You get back to
work, but your hand (A)[accepts / refuses] to move.
After ⓐwasting a few more hours, you decide to
call it a day. As you reach for the power button on
your computer, your mind starts to wander, and...
“Eureka!” The perfect design pops into your head!
This (B)[sudden / gradual] discovery, insight, or
inspiration is called a eureka moment. The Greek
word eureka translates to “I have found it.” This
expression comes from a famous story from ancient
Greece. A king asked a mathematician named
Archimedes ⓑto check if his crown was made of
pure gold. Archimedes tried everything but could
not come up with a solution. To cool his head, he
stepped into a bath. Seeing the water overflow, he
realized at that moment that he could measure the
purity of the crown by putting it in water. He
jumped out of the bath, ⓒscreaming, “Eureka! Eureka!”
A eureka moment may seem miraculous, but that
is (C)[close to / far from] the truth. ⓓIt is the result
of a long process in which ideas form, mix, and
develop. ⓔWhether you’re a mathematician or a
student, here are some strategies to maximize your
chances of having a eureka moment.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: refusesgradual    far from
acceptsgradual    close to
refusessudden    far from
acceptssudden    far from
refusessudden    close to
solution: (A) 다시 작업으로 돌아갔다는 내용 뒤에 역접의 but으로 이어 지므로, 일을 다시 시작했으나 잘 되지 않는다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 손이 움직이는 것을 '거부한다(refuse)'가 적절하다. (B) This ~ inspiration은 앞 문단에서 교내 동아리 포스터의 새로운 디자인을 구상하기 위해 애를 썼으나 시간을 허비하고 결국 컴퓨터의 전원을 끄려던 순간에 아이디어가 떠오른 유레 카를 가리키고 있으므로, '갑작스러운(sudden)' 발견이나 통찰, 영감이라는 흐름이 알맞다. (C) 앞 절에 역접의 but으로 이어지고 있을 뿐만 아니라 뒤에 그것은 사실 기나긴 과정의 결과라고 언급되고 있으므로, 유레 카의 순간이 기적처럼 보일 수 있다는 앞 절의 내용은 사실과 ‘거리가 먼‘ 또는 ’전혀 사실이 아닌‘ 것이라는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 ‘전혀 ~이 아닌, ~와 거리가 먼'의 의미를 갖는 far from이 알맞다.

Stop and Smell the Roses
A brain that is well rested is often the most
efficient one. Are you familiar with the song
Yesterday by the Beatles? It has been called the
greatest song of the 20th century, and its melody
came to a band member in his sleep! After
performing many concerts, Paul McCartney was very
tired and fell asleep. In his dream, he heard a
beautiful melody. He woke up and played it on his
piano, and the rest is history. A eureka moment like
this one cannot come from ⓐ______________________.
If you are stressed and your mind is filled with
thoughts, the chance of a eureka moment is low. If,
however, your mind is ⓑ______________________, there
is more room for new ideas to enter. Going for a
walk in the park, treating yourself to a warm cup of
tea, or maybe even taking a steaming shower might
be just what you need for a eureka moment.

Push Harder: Intense Work Leads to CreativeAchievements

The Power of Imagination in Art

____________________________. Are you familiar with the

I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field
athlete. My room was full of medals and awards
from races I had competed in. During the national
100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic
dreams came to a sudden ⓐend. I was about to
take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain
in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be
carried off the track. At first, I didn’t think much of
the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the
test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The
doctors said my knee injury would ⓑprotect me from
running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of my
injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it
was just too painful. So I shut out everything
ⓒunrelated to sports from my life. Two years passed
and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary
high school life without sports. Then one day, I came
across an interesting university major called sports
medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention
of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head.
This was my chance to ⓓstop running away from my
problems and fears. So I made up my mind and
applied to this major. Today, thanks to my ⓔbrave
decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines
instead of on the playing field.

One evening, I went to a convenience store to

body:
Yuna
Ever since I was young, I have admired great public
speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like
them someday. But every time I had a chance to
speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn’t
want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me
behind the stage rather than on it. That’s why I
never entered the annual speech contest at my
school. I really wanted to, but I just didn’t have
enough courage. Last year, however, was my final
chance before graduating from high school. When I
saw the poster on the class board, my mind began
to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I
heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying “Go
for it!” I decided to sign up for the contest. To make
a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to
the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don’t
remember much from the contest because I was so
nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable
lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

Most people agree with the idea that recycling is
an easy way to make a positive impact on the
planet. It makes you feel good about (A)[you /
yourself], too. But your efforts may sometimes be
harming the environment instead. How can this be?
Well, it is because you might be a wishcycler.
Imagine the following situation. On your way
home from school, someone hands you a piece of
paper. You glance at the shiny flyer advertising a
new study café. As you are about to throw it into
the garbage, you decide to put it into the recycling
bin instead. You think (B)[that / which] flyers can be
recycled because they’re made of paper. What just
happened is a case of wishcycling. It is the act of
trying to recycle something that should not be
recycled. Wishcycling is usually done with good
intentions, (C)[caused / causing] more harm than
good.

(B)
(C)

youwhichcausing

(B) 동사 think의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절(flyers ~ recycled) 을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that이 알맞다. (C) 완전한 절(Wishcycling ~ intentions) 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤 마로만 동사가 이어질 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이뤄야 한다. 따라서 의미상 주어 Wishcyciling이 ‘유발하는’ 주체이므로 능 동을 나타내는 현재분사 causing이 알맞다.

The biggest problem with wishcycling is that it
creates more waste. For example, if you wishcycle a
greasy pizza box, it can ⓐsoak clean paper
products with oil. Then everything in the recycling
bin will become non-recyclable and ⓑend up in a
landfill. Creating more waste is not the only
problem, however. Wishcycling also leads to ⓒcostly
delays. To process recyclable items, non-recyclable
items must be ⓓsorted out first. The more
non-recyclable items are mixed with recyclable
items, the longer it will take to pick them out.
Wishcycled items can also damage the sorting
machines, causing them to be ⓔtemporarily shut
down for repairs.

home from school, someone ⓐhands you a piece
of paper. You glance at the shiny flyer advertising a
new study café. As you are about to throw it into
the garbage, you decide to put it into the recycling
bin instead. You think flyers can be recycled
because they’re made of paper. What just happened
is a case of wishcycling. It is the act of trying to
recycle something that should not be recycled.
Wishcycling is usually done with good ⓑintentions,
but it often causes more harm than good.
The biggest problem with wishcycling is that it
creates more waste. For example, if you wishcycle a
greasy pizza box, it can ⓒsoak clean paper
products with oil. Then everything in the recycling
bin will become non-recyclable and end up in a

delays. To process recyclable items, non-recyclable
items
must
be
sorted
out
first.
The
more

down for repairs.

Good afternoon, students. Today, I’d like to talk
about a topic that concerns us all: Money! Do you
think that you spend money wisely? The truth is
ⓐwhat most people are not as rational as they
think. This is because human beings are easily
influenced
by
psychological

me

In

Steve
Jobs

dollars,” which most people ⓒassuming meant ＄999.
He went on to talk about the features of the tablet
and continued to justify why the tablet was worth
buying. At the end, he said, “I am thrilled to announce
to you that the pricing starts not at ＄999 but at
just ＄499.” The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly
seemed ⓓaffordable to everyone. He put the ＄999
price tag in people’s minds at the beginning so
that the ＄499 price would seem a lot cheaper in

anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works
because people tend to rely on the first piece of

body:
The Endowment Effect
Now let’s move on to another interesting effect. In
an experiment, one group of students was given a
coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar.
Both groups were told they could exchange their
items. A third group wasn’t given anything and was
told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee
mug. This group showed an equal preference for
the two items. (A) About half of the group chose
the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee
mug. (B) This suggested that roughly half of the
first and second groups would trade their items. (C)
But that’s not what happened. (D) Why is this? (E)
This is because people value something more when
they own it. This is the basic idea of the endowment
effect. People are less likely to give up what they
already have or trade it for something else.

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the
ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t
seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all
clocks strike thirteen here. What’s more, the number
thirteen is often associated with bad luck in

called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language to limit people’s thoughts and
expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania,
watches everything that goes on through television
screens. As long as Big Brother is (B)________________,
the people of Oceania will never be free. The main
character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what
the government is doing. He wants to fight against
Big Brother, but he can’t do it by himself. Will
Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in
and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of
the people?

“There is no lake at Camp Green Lake.” - Holes,
Louis Sachar
What comes to mind when you hear the word

like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under
the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you
imagine Camp Green Lake is?

are expected to improve their character by
digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that
there is another reason for the digging. Will
Stanley successfully dig up the truth about
Camp Green Lake?
(B) In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all.
Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad
boys. The main character of the book, a
teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different
from the other boys in the camp. He hasn’t
done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong
place at the wrong time.
(C) Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green
forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line
of Holes paints a different picture. It states that
there is no lake there despite its name. Through
this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green
Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution:
1. 주어진 글은 '캠프'라는 말에서 떠오르는 즐거운 활동을 말한 뒤, Camp Green Lake는 어떤 곳일지 묻는다.
2. (C)는 그 물음을 받아, 아름다운 호수가 있는 곳일 것 같지만 소설 첫 문장이 호수가 없다고 해 평범한 캠프가 아님을 암시한다고 한다.
3. (B)는 In fact로 이어 받아, 그곳이 사실 캠프가 아니라 감옥 같은 곳이고 주인공 Stanley는 아무 잘못도 없다고 소개한다.
4. (A)는 Stanley와 소년들이 매일 구덩이를 파며, Stanley가 그 이유를 의심한다는 내용으로 이어진다.
5. 따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
You never get a second chance to make a first
impression. It is very important to make a good
(A)impression on others when we meet them for
the first time. But people aren’t the only ones who
make first impressions — books do as well. A
powerful first line of a book can catch readers’
attention and make them want to read on. Authors
often spend weeks, months, or even years coming
up with the perfect opening line for their books.
Let’s take a look at some of them.
“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks
were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is (B)out of the ordinary.
But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t seem to be
unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike
thirteen here. What’s more, the number thirteen is
often associated with bad luck in Western cultures.
In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are
about to enter a world that is dark and (C)unfamiliar.
The story takes place in an (D)imaginary country
called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language to limit people’s thoughts and expressions.
Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything
that goes on through television screens. As long as
Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will
never be free. The main character, Winston Smith,
does not agree with what the government is doing.
He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can’t
do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join
him? Or will he (E)give in and be controlled by Big
Brother like the rest of the people?

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): a strong effect or feeling that something makeson someone
(B): unusual or different from what is typical orexpected
(C): unknown or not experienced before
(D): creative and able to come up with new andoriginal ideas
(E): to stop resisting or to yield to someone orsomething after a period of struggle or resistance
solution: (D) ‘상상의, 가상의’의 영영풀이는 'existing only in the mind or in stories, and not in reality’ (실제로 존재하지 않고, 오직 마음이나 이야기 속에만 존재하는)으로 풀이되지만, ‘creative and able to come up with new and original ideas (창의적이고 새롭고 독창적인 아이디어를 생각해 낼 수 있는)’은 Imaginative (상상력이 풍부한)의 영영풀이이다.

body:
You never get a second chance to make a first
impression. It is very important to make a good
(A)impression on others when we meet them for
the first time. But people aren’t the only ones who
make first impressions — books do as well. A
powerful first line of a book can catch readers’
attention and make them want to read on. Authors
often spend weeks, months, or even years coming
up with the perfect opening line for their books.
Let’s take a look at some of them.
“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks
were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is (B)out of the ordinary.
But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t seem to be
unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike
thirteen here. What’s more, the number thirteen is
often associated with bad luck in Western cultures.
In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are
about to enter a world that is dark and (C)unfamiliar.
The story takes place in an (D)imaginary country
called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language to limit people’s thoughts and expressions.
Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything
that goes on through television screens. As long as
Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will
never be free. The main character, Winston Smith,
does not agree with what the government is doing.
He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can’t
do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join
him? Or will he (E)give in and be controlled by Big
Brother like the rest of the people?

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Lost in Time: The Uneasy Opening of 1984
Thirteen Strikes: Unveiling the Dark World of 1984
Winston’s Struggle: Resisting Big Brother’s Control
Why the First Line Still Falls Short of CaptivatingReaders
The Power of the Opening Line: Sustaining Readers’Interest in 1984
solution: 책에도 첫 번째 인상이 얼마나 중요한지 적용된다는 점을 강조 하며, 독자들을 사로잡고 계속 읽게 만드는 완벽한 첫 문장들 중 하나인 소설 1984의 강렬한 첫 문장이 독자들에게 어둡고 생소한 세계로 곧 들어가게 된다는 암시를 주면서 독자들의 관 심을 사로잡고 있음을 설명하며, 주인공인 윈스턴이 다른 사람 들처럼 빅 브라더에게 굴복하고 조종당하게 될지 맞서 싸울지 의문을 남기고 있는 글이다. 따라서 글의 제목으로 ❺ ‘첫 문장 의 힘: 1984에서 독자들의 관심을 유지하기’가 가장 알맞다. 동아(이병민) 2과

body:
“All children, except one, grow up.” - Peter Pan,
J.M. Barrie
No one can stop the sands of time. Every child
becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But
the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is
one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter
Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants
to have fun and stay a child forever.
One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell
visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter
Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky
called Neverland. It is a magical place where
dreams are born and excitement never ends. The
children take Peter Pan’s hand and their adventure
begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they
do not grow up as long as they remain there. They
have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end,
the three children decide to return home and grow
up. What is the reason for this unexpected
decision? Read the book to find out.

윗글의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to convey the importance of the first line inPeter Pan and encourage reading the story
to explain the characteristics of fantasy literaturethrough Peter Pan
to explain the lack of logic of the opening linein Peter Pan
to criticize the unrealistic elements in Peter Pan
to discuss the impact of Peter Pan on literature

public speakers. I hoped to (A)[inspire / respire] and
move audiences like them someday. But every time
I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would
get scared. I didn’t want to make a fool of myself.
This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on
it. That’s why I never (B)[entered / avoided] the
annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted
to, but I just didn’t have enough courage. Last year,
however, was my final chance before graduating
from high school. When I saw the poster on the
class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of
the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing
(C)[fainter / louder] in my head, saying “Go for it!” I
decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long
story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the
entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don’t

nervous. But my act of courage taught me a
valuable lesson: (D)_____________________________________.

solution: (A) Yuna는 어렸을 때부터 대중 연설가들을 동경해왔다고 했 으므로, 언젠가 그들처럼 청중에게 ‘영감을 주고’ 감동을 전하 고 싶었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 move와 뜻을 같이 이 루는 inspire(영감을 주다)가 알맞다. (B) Yuna의 두려움은 무대 뒤에 머물게 했다고 했으므로, 매년 열리는 웅변대회에 ‘참가할’ 용기가 부족했다는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 부정어 never로 보아 entered(참가했다)가 알맞다. (C) Yuna는 대회에 참가하여 학교 전체를 대상으로 연설을 했 다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, Yuna의 머릿속에 한 번 해보라 는 점점 더 크게 말하는 목소리가 들렸다는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 louder(점점 더 커지는)가 알맞다.

body:
The Endowment Effect
Now let’s move on to ⓐanother interesting effect.
In an experiment, one group of students ⓑwas
given a coffee mug and a second group a
chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could
exchange their items. A third group wasn’t given
anything and was told to choose either a chocolate
bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal
preference for the two items. About half of the
group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half
chose the coffee mug. This suggested ⓒwhat
roughly half of the first and second groups would
trade their items. But that’s not what ⓓwas
happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in
the first and second groups were willing to make
the exchange. Why is this? This is because people
value something more when they own it. This is the
basic idea of the endowment effect. People are less
likely to give up what they already have or trade
ⓔit for something else.

Let’s say you are shopping for a new jacket and
the first one you see is priced at $100. That’s too
expensive, as you don’t want to spend more than
$50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a
different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it’s
affordable, even though the price is still beyond
your budget. This is because the first piece of
information acts as an anchor (A)[what / which]
influences your decisions later.
Here’s another common example. Look at the two
pairs of sneakers. They both are $50, but the way
their price (B)[is presented / presented] is different.
Naturally, people are more drawn to the second
pair. This is because the original price serves as an
anchor, ⓐ_______________________________________________.
It is common for stores (C)[to use / use] this kind
of price anchoring as a way to encourage purchases.

(C)

(B) but 뒤에 이어지는 절의 주어 the way에 대한 동사로 is가 있으므로, the way를 수식하는 절의 주어 their price에 대한 동사 자리이며, 주어가 ‘제시되는’ 대상이므로 수동태인 is presented가 적절하다. Good afternoon, students. Today, I’d like to talk
about a topic that concerns us all: Money! Do you
think that you spend money wisely? The truth is
that most people are not as rational as they think.
This is because human beings are easily influenced
by psychological factors. Let me ⓐillustrate my
point through the following examples.
In
2010,
Steve
Jobs
introduced
the
tablet
computer to the world. During the presentation, he
said, “We’re going to price it under a thousand
dollars,” which most people assumed meant ＄999.
He went on to talk about the features of the tablet
and continued to ⓑjustify why the tablet was worth
buying. At the end, he said, “I am thrilled to
announce to you that the pricing starts not at ＄999
but at just ＄499.” The crowd went ⓒwild. The
tablet suddenly seemed affordable to everyone. He
put the ＄999 price tag in people’s minds at the
beginning ⓓso that the ＄499 price would seem a
lot
cheaper
in
comparison.
Steve
Jobs
used
something
called the
anchoring
effect
to his
advantage here. It works because people tend to
ⓔrely on the first piece of information they receive
when making decisions.

creates more waste. For example, if you wishcycle a
greasy pizza box, it can soak clean paper products
with oil. Then everything in the recycling bin will
become non-recyclable and end up in a landfill.
Creating more waste is not the only problem,
however. Wishcycling also leads to costly delays.

/ temporarily] shut down for repairs.

(B) ’골라내다’의 뜻을 가진 pick out은 이어동사(phrasal verb) 로서 목적어가 대명사일 때는 반드시 동사와 부사 사이에 둬야 하고, 목적어가 명사일 때는 동사와 부사 사이 또는 뒤에 올 수도 있다. 따라서 pick them out이 되는 them out이 알맞다. (C) be의 보어가 아니라, to부정사의 수동형 to be p.p.에서 be 와 과거분사 shut 사이에 위치한 형태로, 동사를 수식하는 부 사 temporarily가 알맞다.

impression. It is very important to make a good
impression on others when we meet them for the
first time. But people aren’t the only ones who
make first impressions — books do as well. A
powerful first line of a book can catch readers’
attention and make them want to read on. Authors
often spend weeks, months, or even years coming
up with the perfect opening line for their books.
Let’s take a look at some of them.
“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks
were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is ⓐextraordinary.
But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t seem to be
unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike
thirteen here. What’s more, the number thirteen is
often associated with bad luck in Western cultures.
In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they
are ⓑreluctant to enter a world that is dark and
unfamiliar.
The story takes place in an imaginary country
called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language to limit people’s thoughts and
expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania,
watches everything that goes on through television
screens. As long as Big Brother is in ⓒauthority,
the people of Oceania will never be free. The main
character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what
the government is doing. He wants to ⓓoppose Big
Brother, but he can’t do it by himself. Will Winston
find others to join him? Or will he ⓔsurrender and
be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the
people?

were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But
George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, ⓐopening
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary.
But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t seem ⓑto
be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike
thirteen here. What’s more, the number thirteen is
often associated with bad luck in Western cultures.
In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are
about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.
The story takes place in an imaginary country ⓒwhich
called Oceania in the year 1984. The government
tries to control everyone’s life. It has even created a
new language to limit people’s thoughts and
expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania,
watches everything ⓓthat goes on through television
screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people
of Oceania will never be free. The main character,
Winston Smith, does not agree with ⓔwhat the
government is doing. He wants to fight against Big

Both groups were told they could exchange their items.
A third group wasn’t given anything and was told
to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug.
(A) This is because people value something more

endowment effect. People are less likely to give
up what they already have or trade it for
something else.

percent of the students in the first and second

mug. This suggested that roughly half of the

“It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks
were striking thirteen.” - 1984, George Orwell
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times.
But George Orwell’s well-known novel, 1984, opens
with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal
world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the
ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn’t
seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all
clocks strike thirteen here. What’s more, the number
thirteen is often associated with bad luck in
Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the
readers that they are about to enter a world that is

Olivia
I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field
athlete. My room was full of medals and awards
from races I had competed in. During the national
100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic
dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take
the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in
my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried
off the track. At first, I didn’t think much of the
injury. I thought I would ⓐget better soon. But the
test results from the hospital were not ⓑhopeless.
The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me
from running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of
my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because
it was just too painful. So I ⓒshut out everything
related to sports from my life. Two years passed and
I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high
school life without sports. Then one day, I came
across an ⓓinteresting university major called sports
medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention
of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head.
This was my chance to stop running away from my
problems and fears. So I made up my mind and
applied to this major. Today, thanks to my ⓔbrave
decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines
instead of on the playing field.

putting

in

(A)

solution: (A) Jason은 점원이 바닥에 누워 있는 것을 보고 즉시 911에 전화를 걸어 상황을 설명했다고 했으며, 뒤로 Jason은 겁이 났 지만 학교에서 심폐소생술을 배운 것이 떠올라 점원의 가슴을 누르기 시작했다고 했으므로, 교환원은 구급대가 도착할 때까 지 점원에게 심폐소생술을 ‘해달라고’ 요청했다는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 따라서 ‘수행하다’라는 뜻의 undertake가 알맞다. (B) Jason이 911에 신고한 후, 심폐소생술을 했고, 구급대원들 이 뛰어들어와 점원을 구급차에 태웠다고 했으므로 상황을 ‘넘 겨받았다’라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘넘겨받았다, 인계받 다’라는 뜻의 took over가 알맞다. (C) 구급대원들이 도착할 때까지 쓰러진 점원에게 심폐소생술을 수행해 준 Jason에게 구급대원들이 훌륭한 일을 해냈다고 말하 고 있으므로 ‘용감하게’ 행동해 주어 고맙다고 인사했다는 흐름 이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘용감한’의 뜻을 가진 valiant가 알맞다.

The biggest problem with wishcycling is that it
creates more waste. For example, if you wishcycle a
greasy pizza box, it can soak clean paper products
with oil. Then everything in the recycling bin will
become non-recyclable and end up in a landfill.
Creating more waste is not the only problem,
however. Wishcycling also ____________________________.
To process recyclable items, non-recyclable items
must be sorted out first. The more non-recyclable
items are mixed with recyclable items, the longer it
will take to pick them out. Wishcycled items can
also damage the sorting machines, causing them to
be temporarily shut down for repairs.

triggers the need for environmental education

leads to costly delays

(C) 좋은 의도로 행해졌다는 앞 절에 but으로 이어지고 있으므 로 실은 좋지 않다는 내용이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘이로움보다 는 해로움‘을 야기한다는 흐름이 되도록, 'B라기보다 A인‘의 의 미를 갖는 more A than B의 표현을 사용해야 한다. 따라서 more이 흐름상 알맞다.

This wonderful display of warmth happens at every
University of Iowa football team home game. The
tradition started in 2017 with a social media post
by Krista Young, an Iowa football fan and a mother
of three children. ⓐWhile browsed the internet, she
came across photos of the newly built children’s
hospital next to the University of Iowa stadium. The
new hospital overlooked the stadium, so the
children were able to see what was going on
inside. Then a simple idea came to Krista. She
posted a message on the social media fan page of
the athletic teams of the University of Iowa.
“I think the stadium should hold a ‘wave to the
kids’ minute during every game. Just imagine how
amazing it would be if all the fans, players, and
coaching staff were looking up at the children at
the hospital sending a little extra inspiration.”
And it just took fire. The page’s administrator
promoted the idea to the followers and ⓑasked the
hospital send him photos of the children looking
over the stadium. When he received the photos, he
used them to make online posts to give the idea
momentum.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Who started the tradition of the ‘wave to the kids’at the University of Iowa’s home football games?
Why was the children’s hospital built next tothe stadium?
Why were the children at the hospital able tosee what was happening in the stadium?
How did the administrator help spread the idea?

The message of the wave is incredibly significant:
“We see you. We know you’re there. We (A)[know /
overlook] you’re going through a hard time. We
support you.” The children wave back, smiling brightly.
Their eyes shine with joy. It is their moment. It is a
moment of connection, encouragement, and hope.
Although this event started in 2017, it has already
become a tradition. On Saturdays in fall, kids in the
hospital go up to the 12th-floor window no matter
what. For night games, people turn on the flashlights
on their phones to participate in the wave.
This touching event has attracted a lot of attention
across the U.S., (B)[encouraging / forbidding] other
college football teams to participate. Now it is one
of the best traditions in college football. How long
will this tradition continue? As long as there is
hope, the wave will (C)[fade away / live on].

(C)

solution: (A) 손짓이 전하는 메시지가 ‘우리는 너희를 보고 있어. 우리는 너희가 거기에 있다는 것을 알아. 우리는 너희를 응원해’이므 로 아이들이 힘든 시간을 보내고 있다는 걸 알고 있다는 흐름 이 자연스럽다. 따라서 know(알다)가 적절하다. (B) 다음 문장에서 손 흔들기가 ‘대학 미식축구에 있어 최고의 전통 중 하나이다’라고 했으므로 다른 대학의 미식축구팀들이 참여하도록 장려했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 encourage (장려하다)가 적절하다. (C) 손 흔들기가 미국 전역에서 많은 관심을 받았고, 대학 미 식축구의 최고의 전통 중 하나라고 했으므로 손 흔들기는 많은 사람들에게 긍정적인 영향을 주는 것임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 희망이 존재하는 한 손 흔들기는 계속될 것이라는 흐름이 자 연스러우므로 live on((전통·기억 등이) 오래 남다)이 적절하다.

My name is Jiwoo, and I’m a first-year student at
Hankook High School. Two things I truly love ⓐare
animals
and
travel.
I
used
to
watch
nature
documentaries
as
a
child
and
have
always
ⓑfascinated by different animals around the world.
So, when I saw a poster about a volunteer camp in
Kenya, I knew this was ⓒwhat I wanted to do
during my summer break.
Day 1
When I arrived at the airport in Nairobi, Kenya’s
capital, I got my first taste of Kenya — busy, exciting,
and warm. When I went outside, I was greeted by
the camp supervisor, Henry. Other volunteers from
different countries also arrived at similar times, and
we started making new friends right away.
We got into a large van and drove around the
crowded city. Although English is widely ⓓspoken
in Kenya, the people here also use Swahili. The first
Swahili word we learned was jambo, ⓔwhich means
“hello.”

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Jiwoo has loved animals and traveling since childhood.
Jiwoo decided to join the Kenya volunteer campafter seeing a poster.
The camp supervisor Henry welcomed Jiwoo atthe Nairobi airport.
People in Kenya use only one language in dailylife.
Jiwoo learned the Swahili word jambo soon afterarriving in Kenya.

body:
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National
Museum, where I became (A)[fascinating / fascinated]
by the diverse cultural and natural heritage of
Kenya. Going from hall to hall, I learned about
Kenya’s many natural resources and animals, different
communities and languages, and even important
artists. One of the most ⓐimpressive displays
(B)[was / were] the statue of Ahmed, an elephant
with massive tusks. It ⓑsymbolizes the movement
against illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we headed to
the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy (C)[which / where]
we would begin our volunteer work. There, several
impalas were waiting to welcome us. The camp
house was made of stone and olive wood. After an
amazing day, I fell asleep the minute my head hit
the pillow.
Day 2
In the morning, volunteers were told what they
were going to do. I was assigned to “the giraffe
survey” group. At the conservancy, there were 26
giraffes. All of them had names and could be
ⓒidentified by the spots on their bodies. Like the
human fingerprint, the pattern of spots on a giraffe
is ⓓuniversal. ㉠우리 그룹의 임무는 카메라들과 쌍안
경들을 사용해 기린들을 찾아서 식별하는 것이었다.
Then we had to record their locations and activities.
We often needed to take pictures of both sides of
the animal for identification. It wasn’t easy. This
required us to go around the giraffe to the other
side before it ran away. Later, back at the camp,
we had to compare our photos of the giraffes with
the ones in the identification book. We not only
successfully identified most of the giraffes but also
ⓔdiscovered new baby giraffes that were not in the
book yet!

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: fascinated   was    which
fascinated   were     which
fascinated   was    where
fascinating   were     where
fascinating   was    which
solution: (A) 2형식 동사 became의 주격보어 자리이며, 주어인 I가 ‘매료된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사형 형용사 fascinated 가 적절하다. (B) 주어로 ‘One of+최상급+복수명사구’가 쓰였으며, 주어의 핵은 One으로 단수이므로 단수동사인 was가 적절하다. (C) 뒤에 완전한 절(we would ~ work)이 이어지고 있으므로, 장소를 나타내는 선행사 the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy를  수 식하는 관계사절을 이루는 관계부사 where이 적절하다. which 뒤에는 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다.

body:
Day 1
When I arrived at the airport in Nairobi, Kenya’s
capital, I got my first taste of Kenya — busy, exciting,
and warm. When I went outside, I was greeted by
the camp supervisor, Henry. Other volunteers from
different countries also arrived at similar times, and
we started making new friends right away.
We got into a large van and drove around the
crowded city. Although English is widely spoken in
Kenya, the people here also use Swahili. The first
Swahili word we learned was jambo, which means
“hello.”
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National
Museum, where I became fascinated by the diverse
cultural and natural heritage of Kenya. Going from
hall to hall, I learned about Kenya’s many natural
resources and animals, different communities and
languages, and even important artists. One of the
most impressive displays was the statue of Ahmed,
an elephant with massive tusks. It symbolizes the
movement against illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we
headed to the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy where we
would begin our volunteer work. There, several
impalas were waiting to welcome us. The camp
house was made of stone and olive wood. After an
amazing day, I fell asleep the minute my head hit
the pillow.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: language differences experienced by internationalvolunteers
the beginning of a meaningful volunteer journeyin Kenya
the importance of wildlife conservation efforts inKenya
my volunteer work in Kenya’s wildlife conservancy
a tourist’s visit to famous landmarks in Nairobi
solution: 글쓴이가 자원 봉사자들과 처음 만나고, 나이로비 국립 박물관 에서 케냐의 문화와 자연 유산을 접하며, 본격적인 자원봉사 활동 장소인 키기오 야생 동물 보호 구역에 도착하기까지의 과정을 다루고 있는 글이다. 따라서 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것 은 ❷ ‘케냐에서 의미 있는 자원봉사 여정의 시작’이다.

This wonderful display of warmth happens at every
University of Iowa football team home game. The
tradition started in 2017 with a social media post
by Krista Young, an Iowa football fan and a mother
of three children. While browsing the internet, she
came across photos of the newly built children’s
hospital next to the University of Iowa stadium. The
new hospital overlooked the stadium, so the
children were able to see what was going on
inside. Then a simple idea came to Krista. She
posted a message on the social media fan page of
the athletic teams of the University of Iowa.
“I think the stadium should hold a ‘wave to the
kids’ minute during every game. Just imagine how
amazing it would be if all the fans, players, and
coaching staff were looking up at the children at
the hospital sending a little extra inspiration.”
And it just took fire. The page’s administrator promoted
the idea to the followers and asked the hospital to
send him photos of the children looking over the
stadium. When he received the photos, he used them
to make online posts to give the idea momentum.

team plays at home, this touching act of
kindness occurs. (T/F)

of Iowa’s coaching staff in 2017. (T/F)

stadium, Krista posted the idea of fans waving
to the watching children on social media. (T/F)
(D) After the fan page administrator informed
Krista’s idea, it spread quickly online. (T/F)
(E) Krista sent the photos of the children to the
fan page administrator herself. (T/F)

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Stress Eating
You have a big test tomorrow. There are many
things to memorize, and you don’t feel prepared at
all. Looking at the piles of books in front of you,
you begin to crave something spicy!
When stressed, many people naturally turn to food,
especially strong-tasting food such as tteokbokki or
spicy chicken. This is an example of stress eating.
Stress eaters use food to make themselves feel
better. They try to escape reality for a while by
eating food with a strong flavor. But never will it
lead to solutions to their problems. It will lead only
to an upset stomach or feelings of guilt and shame.
To avoid being a stress eater, try to move yourself
away from food and find other ways to relieve your
stress. For example, you could go for a walk, talk to
a friend, or watch your favorite TV show. If you still
want something to eat, treat yourself to whole-grain
toast or a nice cup of tea.
choices: People often reach for strong-tasting food whenthey are under stress.
Eating food to relieve stress may be a quickand easy way to feel calm.
Stress eating can lead to feelings of guilt andshame afterward.
It's better to find healthier ways to deal withstress than relying on food.
Taking a walk or enjoying a cup of tea canhelp relieve stress.

5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The bell rings. Thrilled students rush
to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is gone in the blink
of an eye, but are they really satisfied?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to eat too much
(A)[before / after] they realize they are full.
Moreover, speed eating (B)[offers / takes away] the
experience of appreciating the pleasures of a good
meal. Although it may seem advantageous to save
some time from your busy schedule by eating
quickly, slowing down your meals actually has more
(C)[benefits / drawbacks]. Give yourself at least 20
minutes to eat your meals. Take smaller bites and
chew your food for a longer time. Not only will
eating slower prevent you from eating too much,
but it will also help you appreciate all the flavors of
your food.

solution: (A) 음식을 눈 깜짝할 사이에 먹어 치운 학생들이 정말로 만족 하는지에 대한 질문에 아마도 그렇지 않을 것이다(Probably not)라고 했으므로, ‘배가 부르다는 것을 깨닫기 전에 너무 많 이 먹는 경향이 있다.’라는 내용이 자연스럽기 때문에 before(~ 전에)가 알맞다. (B) 빨리 먹는 사람들에 대한 부정적인 내용을 Moreover로 추 가하고 있으므로, 식사를 빨리 하면 맛있는 식사의 즐거움을 느낄 수 있는 경험을 빼앗아간다는 내용이 자연스럽기 때문에 takes away(빼앗다)가 알맞다. (C) Although가 이끄는 절에서 ‘빨리 먹음으로써 시간을 절약 하는 것이 이롭게 보일 수도 있지만‘이라고 말하며 역접 구조 로 이어져야 하므로 ’천천히 먹는 것이 더 많은 이점이 있다‘라 는 내용이 되어야 한다. 따라서 benefits(혜택, 이득)가 알맞다.

with a bag of potato chips in one hand and your

aware of the food you are putting into your mouth.

from the oven. The ⓐheavenly smell and the rich
chocolate melting in your mouth are sure to make
your mouth water. The human body is designed to
ⓑcrave sweets. Sugar is a quick source of energy
for our body. It also ⓒtriggers our brains to
ⓓrelease chemicals that make us feel good. Not
only that, it’s delicious, too! However, if you are
unable to go a single day without sweets, you need
to control your sweet tooth. It doesn’t mean you
have to stop eating sugary snacks completely.

bar, can slow down your sugar cravings. Instead of
sugary snacks, try healthier ⓔalternatives such as
fruit or dark chocolate.

You have a big test tomorrow. There are many
things to memorize, and you don’t feel prepared at
all. Looking at the piles of books in front of you,
you begin to crave something spicy!
When stressed, many people naturally turn to food,
especially strong-tasting food such as tteokbokki or
spicy chicken. This is an example of stress eating.
Stress eaters use food to make themselves feel
better. They try to escape reality for a while by
eating food with a strong flavor. (A)______________
never will it lead to solutions to their problems. It
will lead only to an upset stomach or feelings of guilt
and shame. To avoid being a stress eater, try to
move yourself away from food and find other ways
to relieve your stress. (B)______________, you could go
for a walk, talk to a friend, or watch your favorite
TV show. If you still want something to eat, treat
yourself to whole-grain toast or a nice cup of tea.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What do stress eaters hope to achieve byeating certain foods?
What are some possible side effects of stresseating?
What kinds of food do people crave when theyfeel stressed?
What advice is given to avoid relying on foodwhen feeling stressed?
Why do people believe that eating spicy foodhelps relieve stress?

the hospital

at the children’s hospital across the street from the
stadium. The children and their families, gathered
together in a special room on the 12th floor of the
hospital, ⓑwaving back. The people in the stadium
cheer at the top of their voices and wave even more
energetically. Most of these children don’t have
much ⓒto smile about, since they are going through
tough times at the hospital. But today, during this
special moment, their faces light up with joy.
This wonderful display of warmth happens at every
University of Iowa football team home game. The
tradition started in 2017 with a social media post
by Krista Young, an Iowa football fan and a mother
of three children. ⓓWhile browsing the internet, she
came across photos of the newly built children’s
hospital next to the University of Iowa stadium. The
new hospital overlooked the stadium, so the
children were able to see ⓔwhat was going on
inside. Then a simple idea came to Krista. She
posted a message on the social media fan page of
the athletic teams of the University of Iowa.
“I think the stadium should hold a ‘wave to the
kids’ minute during every game. Just imagine how
amazing it would be if all the fans, players, and
coaching staff were looking up at the children at
the hospital sending a little extra inspiration.”

body:
Stress Eating
You have a big test tomorrow. There are many
things to memorize, and you don’t feel prepared at
all. Looking at the piles of books in front of you,
you begin to crave something spicy!
When stressed, many people naturally (A)[look to /
avoid] food, especially strong-tasting food such as
tteokbokki or spicy chicken. This is an example of
stress eating. Stress eaters use food to make
themselves feel better. They try to (B)[escape /
confront] reality for a while by eating food with a
strong flavor. But ⓐ그것이 그들의 문제들에 대한 해
결책들로 절대 이어지지 않을 것이다. It will lead
only to an upset stomach or feelings of guilt and
shame. To avoid being a stress eater, try to move
yourself away from food and find other ways to
(C)[alleviate / aggravate] your stress. For example,
you could go for a walk, talk to a friend, or watch
your favorite TV show. If you still want something
to eat, treat yourself to whole-grain toast or a nice
cup of tea.

to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is ⓐgone in the
blink of an eye, but are they really satisfied?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to eat too much
before they realize ⓑthat they are full. Moreover,
speed
eating
takes
away
the
experience
of
appreciating
the
pleasures
of
a
good
meal.
Although it may seem advantageous ⓒto save
some time from your busy schedule by eating
quickly, ⓓslow down your meals actually has more
benefits. Give yourself at least 20 minutes to eat
your meals. Take smaller bites and chew your food
for a longer time. Not only will eating slower ⓔto

could go for a walk, talk to a friend, or watch your

smartphone in the other. ⓓChecking your social

much food you are eating. It usually ends when you

me feel better. Our body tells us we
need food to relax.

eating, you might finish all your food
without realizing it.

solution. If strong-tasting food helps your

to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is gone in the blink
of an eye, but are they really satisfied?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to (A)______________
before they realize they are full. Moreover, speed
eating takes away the experience of appreciating
the pleasures of a good meal. Although ⓐwhat
may seem advantageous to save some time from
your busy schedule by eating quickly, slowing down
your meals actually ⓑhaving more benefits. Give
yourself at least 20 minutes to eat your meals. Take
smaller bites and chew your food for a longer time.
Not only ⓒeating slower will prevent you from
eating too much, but it will also help you
appreciate all the flavors of your food.
Sweet-Tooth Snacking
Imagine biting into a chocolate chip cookie fresh
from the oven. The heavenly smell and the rich
chocolate melting in your mouth are sure to make
your mouth water. The human body is designed to
(B)______________. Sugar is a quick source of energy
for our body. It also triggers our brains to ⓓbe
released chemicals that make us feel good. Not
only that, it’s delicious, too! However, if you are
unable to go a single day without sweets, you need
to control your sweet tooth. It doesn’t mean ⓔwhat
you have to stop eating sugary snacks completely.
Eating smaller portions, such as a fun-size candy
bar, can slow down your sugar cravings. Instead of
sugary snacks, try healthier alternatives such as fruit
or dark chocolate.

body:
You have probably heard the saying, “You are
what you eat.” It means that it is important (A)[eat
/ to eat] good food in order to be healthy. But the
way you eat food is just as important as (B)[eat /
eating] the right food. Many people have bad
eating habits, but they often aren’t aware of them.
Do you have any bad eating habits? Let’s find out
whether you fall into any of the following categories.
Speed Eating
5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The bell rings. Thrilled students rush
to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is gone in the blink
of an eye, but are they really (C)[satisfying /
satisfied]?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to eat too much
before they realize they are full. Moreover, speed
eating takes away the experience of appreciating
the pleasures of a good meal. Although it may
seem advantageous to save some time from your
busy schedule by eating quickly, slowing down your
meals actually has more benefits. Give yourself at
least 20 minutes to eat your meals. Take smaller
bites and chew your food for a longer time. (D)더
천천히 먹는 것은 여러분이 과식하는 것을 막아 줄 뿐
만 아니라 그것은 또한 여러분이 음식의 모든 맛을 느
낄 수 있도록 도와줄 것이다.

to eateating    satisfied
eateat    satisfied

solution: (A) 가주어 it, 동사 is, 보어 important에 이어져 ‘it is+보어(형 용사)+진주어(to부정사)(~하는 것은 …하다)’의 구문을 이루어야 하므로 진주어 자리에 to eat는 적절하다. (B) ‘~만큼 …한’을 뜻하는 원급 비교(as+형용사+as) 구문이 쓰 였으며, 주어인 the way you eat food와 비교 대상이 되어야 하므로, 전치사로 쓰인 두 번째 as 뒤에는 명사 역할을 할 수 있는 동명사 eating이 이어져야 적절하다. (C) 주어인 they(=thrilled students)의 상태를 설명하는 형용사 보어 자리로, 그들이 ‘만족하는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과 거분사 satisfied가 적절하다.

body:
You have probably heard the saying, “You are
what you eat.” It means that it is important (A)[eat
/ to eat] good food in order to be healthy. But the
way you eat food is just as important as (B)[eat /
eating] the right food. Many people have bad
eating habits, but they often aren’t aware of them.
Do you have any bad eating habits? Let’s find out
whether you fall into any of the following categories.
Speed Eating
5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The bell rings. Thrilled students rush
to the school cafeteria. As soon as they get their
food, they eat it as if it’s the last 10 seconds of a
speed-eating contest. The food is gone in the blink
of an eye, but are they really (C)[satisfying /
satisfied]?
Probably not. Speed eaters tend to eat too much
before they realize they are full. Moreover, speed
eating takes away the experience of appreciating
the pleasures of a good meal. Although it may
seem advantageous to save some time from your
busy schedule by eating quickly, slowing down your
meals actually has more benefits. Give yourself at
least 20 minutes to eat your meals. Take smaller
bites and chew your food for a longer time. (D)더

media, you start eating the chips. Suddenly, you

empty bag!
You have just become a prime example of a
mindless eater. Mindless eating happens when you
are distracted and do not pay attention to how
much food you are eating. It usually ends when
you
run

food,

(A)______________, instead of being a mindless eater,

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
choices: In addition   For instance
However   For instance

So   Therefore
However   In other words
solution: (A) 빈칸 앞에서는 생각 없이 먹는 행위의 부정적인 면을 설명 하며, 이러한 식사는 음식을 다 먹었을 때에야 끝나지만 그때 는 이미 늦다고 말하고 있다. 이어지는 빈칸 뒤에서는 의식적 으로 먹는 사람이 되어야 한다고 제안하고 있으므로, 글의 흐 름은 문제에서 해결책으로 이어지는 인과 관계이다. 따라서 빈 칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ‘그러므로(So)’이다. (B) 앞 문장에서 먹는 것에 집중할 수 있을 때에만 먹으라고 했고 빈칸 뒤에서 다른 활동을 하면서 먹지 말라고 했는데, 이 는 앞 문장의 내용을 표현만 바꿔 재진술한 것이므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ‘다시 말해서(In other words)’이다.

Stress Eating
You have a big test tomorrow. There are many
things to memorize, and you don’t feel prepared at
all. Looking at the piles of books in front of you,
you begin to crave something spicy!
When stressed, many people naturally turn to food,
especially strong-tasting food such as tteokbokki or
spicy chicken.
(A) For example, you could go for a walk, talk to a
friend, or watch your favorite TV show. If you
still want something to eat, treat yourself to
whole-grain toast or a nice cup of tea.
(B) But never will it lead to solutions to their
problems. It will lead only to an upset stomach
or feelings of guilt and shame. To avoid being
a stress eater, try to move yourself away from
food and find other ways to relieve your stress.
(C) This is an example of stress eating. Stress eaters
use food to make themselves feel better. They
try to escape reality for a while by eating food
with a strong flavor.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 사람들이 스트레스를 받을 때 떡볶이와 매운 치킨과 같은 자 극적인 맛의 음식을 찾는 경향이 있는데, 이를 This로 받아서 스트레스로 인한 먹기의 예시라고 정의하고, 사람들이 왜 이러 한 행동을 하는지 설명하는 (C), But(그러나)으로 시작하여 이 것이 문제 해결로 이어지지 않고 오히려 신체적, 심리적 부작 용을 가져올 수 있다는 문제점과 해결 방안을 제안하는 (B), 스트레스로 인한 먹기 대신 할 수 있는 구체적인 대안들(산책, 친구와 대화, TV 시청 등)을 For example로 시작하여 소개하 는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
[1]
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National Museum,
where I became fascinated by the diverse cultural and
natural heritage of Kenya. Going from hall to hall, I
learned about Kenya’s many natural resources and
animals, different communities and languages, and
even important artists. One of the most impressive
displays was the statue of Ahmed, an elephant with
massive tusks. It symbolizes the movement against
illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we headed to the Kigio
Wildlife Conservancy where we would begin our
volunteer work. There, several impalas were waiting to
welcome us. The camp house was made of stone and
olive wood. After an amazing day, I fell asleep the
minute my head hit the pillow.
[2]
In the morning, volunteers were told what they
were going to do. I was assigned to “the giraffe
survey” group. At the conservancy, there were 26
giraffes. All of ⓐthem had names and could be
identified by the spots on their bodies. Like the
human fingerprint, the pattern of spots on a giraffe
is unique. Our group’s job was to find the giraffes
and identify ⓑthem using cameras and binoculars.
Then we had to record their locations and activities.
We often needed to take pictures of both sides of
the animal for identification. ⓒIt wasn’t easy. This
required us to go around the giraffe to the other
side before ⓓit ran away. Later, back at the camp,
we had to compare our photos of the giraffes with
the ⓔones in the identification book. We not only
successfully identified most of the giraffes but also
discovered new baby giraffes that were not in the
book yet!

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ가 가리키는 것으로 알맞게연결되지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 26 giraffes
ⓑ: cameras and binoculars
ⓒ: taking pictures of both sides of the animalfor identification
ⓓ: the giraffe
ⓔ: photos
solution: ⓑ는 the giraffes를 가리킨다.

body:
Day 3
My assignment for today was to search for illegal
animal traps on the conservancy. Hunters illegally
set up wire traps and wait for animals to get
caught. (A)[Stop / To stop] this from happening, my
group drove out to the field with some experienced
trap spotters. There, we spread out and looked for
traps. We found a lot of wire traps on the ground.
Some traps were hidden in the bushes and others
were (B)[attaching / attached] to fences. Every time
we found a trap, we were saving the life of an
animal. It was one of the most rewarding moments
during my time in Kenya.
Day 4
Today’s camp dinner was chapati, which is one of
the most popular Kenyan dishes. It’s made with

body:
Day 2
In the morning, volunteers were told what they
were going to do. I was assigned to “the giraffe
survey” group. At the conservancy, there were 26
giraffes. All of them had names and could be
identified by the spots on their bodies. Like the
human fingerprint, the pattern of spots on a giraffe
is unique. Our group’s job was to find the giraffes
and identify them using cameras and binoculars.
Then we had to record their locations and activities.
We often needed to take pictures of both sides of
the animal for identification. It wasn’t easy. ㉠This
required us to go around the giraffe to the other
side before it ran away. Later, back at the camp,
we had to compare our photos of the giraffes with
the ones in the identification book. We not only
successfully identified most of the giraffes but also
discovered new baby giraffes that were not in the
book yet!
Day 3
My assignment for today was to search for illegal
animal traps on the conservancy. Hunters illegally
set up wire traps and wait for animals to get
caught. To stop ㉡this from happening, my group
drove out to the field with some experienced trap
spotters. There, we spread out and looked for traps.
We found a lot of wire traps on the ground. Some
traps were hidden in the bushes and others were
attached to fences. Every time we found a trap, we
were saving the life of an animal. It was one of the
most rewarding moments during my time in Kenya.

locating wire traps (C)______________ set by hunters,
gaining meaningful field experience through both
tasks.
(A)              (B)
(C)

body:
Social media algorithms play a huge role in our
everyday lives. They make our lives easier by
presenting us with options ⓐthat we may be
interested in. Algorithms decide ⓑwhich content is
shown to us. They also determine the order of the
content that ⓒappears on our social media feed. If
we are using an app to watch videos, for example,
we may see suggestions for ⓓrelated videos. These
recommendations are not random. They are based
on our previous activity — what we’ve watched or
clicked on in the past. This information is fed into
an algorithm, ⓔthat then decides what we will see.
Social media algorithms are all around us, but
they are a double-edged sword that can bring both
benefits and problems. Let’s look at some pros and
cons of social media algorithms.

body:
Social media algorithms play a huge role in our
everyday lives. They make our lives easier by
presenting us with options that we may be
interested in. Algorithms decide which content is
shown to us. They also determine the order of the
content that appears on our social media feed. If
we are using an app to watch videos, for example,
we may see suggestions for related videos. These
recommendations are not random. They are based
on our previous activity — what we’ve watched or
clicked on in the past. This information is fed into
an algorithm, ⓐwhich then decides that we will see.
Social media algorithms are all around us, but
ⓑthey are a double-edged sword what can bring
both benefits and problems. Let’s look at some
pros and cons of social media algorithms.

My name is Jiwoo, and I’m a first-year student at
Hankook High School. Two things I truly love are
animals and travel. I used to watch nature documentaries
as a child and ⓐhave always been fascinated by
different animals around the world. So, when I saw a
poster about a volunteer camp in Kenya, I knew this
was what I wanted to do during my summer break.
Day 1
When I arrived at the airport in Nairobi, Kenya’s
capital, I got my first taste of Kenya — busy, exciting,
and warm. When I went outside, I was greeted by
the camp supervisor, Henry. Other volunteers from
different countries also arrived at similar times, and
we started making new friends right away.
We got into a large van and drove around the
crowded city. Although English is widely spoken in
Kenya, the people here also use Swahili. The first Swahili
word we learned was jambo, ⓑwhich means “hello.”
Henry took all of us to the Nairobi National
Museum, ⓒwhere I became fascinated by the diverse
cultural and natural heritage of Kenya. ⓓGoing from
hall to hall, I learned about Kenya’s many natural
resources and animals, different communities and
languages, and even important artists. One of the
most impressive displays was the statue of Ahmed,
an elephant with massive tusks. It symbolizes the
movement against illegal hunting in Kenya. Then we
headed to the Kigio Wildlife Conservancy where we
would begin our volunteer work. There, several impalas
were waiting to welcome us. The camp house was
made of stone and olive wood. After an amazing
day, ⓔI fell asleep the minute my head hit the pillow.

giraffes. All of them had names and could be
identified by the spots on their bodies. Like the
human fingerprint, the pattern of spots on a giraffe
is unique. Our group’s job was to find the giraffes
and identify them using cameras and binoculars. Then
we had to record their locations and activities. We
often needed to take pictures of both sides of the
animal for identification. It wasn’t easy. This required
us to go around the giraffe to the other side before

compare our photos of the giraffes with the ones in

identified most of the giraffes but also discovered
new baby giraffes that were not in the book yet!
Day 3
My assignment for today was to search for illegal
animal traps on the conservancy. Hunters illegally
set up wire traps and wait for animals to get
caught. To stop this from happening, my group
drove out to the field with some experienced trap
spotters. There, we spread out and looked for traps.
We found a lot of wire traps on the ground. Some
traps were hidden in the bushes and others were
attached to fences. Every time we found a trap, we
were saving the life of an animal. It was one of the
most rewarding moments during my time in Kenya.

work. There, several
impalas were waiting to

pictures

book.

more than meets the eye.” It means that there is
more to something than there appears to be at
first. This can apply to art as well. We appreciate
art by looking at its colors, shapes, shadows, as
well as the overall beauty presented by the artist.
Sometimes, however, there is something more to
the images in front of our eyes. Science, which
seems far removed from art, can be (A)______________
________________________________________. Today, I would
like to open your eyes and minds through the
following paintings.
Art Is Never Finished

Rembrandt’s The Night Watch, a huge painting
ⓐthat measures 3.795 meters by 4.535 meters, has
had a troubled history. It was damaged with a knife
twice and sprayed with acid by people who wanted
to destroy it. Each time, experts miraculously
restored the painting to its original state. But did

over three centuries ago? In 1715, this monumental

from the left side, 22 cm from the top, 12 cm from
the bottom, and 7 cm from the right side ⓑhave
been missing.
However, art lovers can now see The Night Watch
as Rembrandt originally intended. It was artificial
intelligence (AI) ⓒthat the museum used to recreate
the missing pieces. Instead of ⓓhiring human artists,
an AI program was trained to learn Rembrandt’s
painting style. Once the AI program learned to
paint like Rembrandt, it was shown a copy of the
original painting before it was trimmed. Then it
reconstructed the missing pieces, which were hung
around the painting. For the first time in over three
centuries, The Night Watch is complete again. Thanks
to science, this great masterpiece ⓔhas been brought
back to life for all to see.

stolen by art thieves
not artistically valuable

Art Is Never Finished
Look at the portrait of a woman on the next

analyzed
by

He
used
special

After careful examination of the layers, it was
revealed that the original painting was just a
normal portrait of a woman by herself. Then in a
second version, a small gray ermine appeared.
Finally in a third version — the one we know today
— the ermine became bigger and its color changed
to white. Why did Da Vinci add the ermine to this
painting? No one knows for sure. He might have
done it to honor his patron. Maybe he just wanted
to make the painting look more special. Whatever
the reason, this shows us that even a great master
like Leonardo da Vinci, who said, “Art is never
finished,” made revisions to his paintings over and
over again.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Through the analysis, it was discovered that thepainting has several layers hidden below thesurface.
It was in the second version that a small grayermine appeared.
Experts are certain that Leonardo da Vinci addedthe ermine to please his patron.
The changing versions of the painting show thatDa Vinci often revised his works.

admit that it lacks creativity.

the way art is created.

insights. It can also help artists add fine details.
I’m excited about how AI will change the future
of art.
